styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Museums, the Barber Institute and canal-side art.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Balti curry, street food and the Jewellery Quarter cafés.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Industrial heritage, canals and the old workshops.

stays.why: Walk to New Street station, the Bullring and the museums. Best base for a first visit.
Canalside bars and restaurants, close to the ICC and the Sea Life centre. Quiet at night.
Historic workshops, small museums and good cafés. A short tram or walk from the centre.
Creative quarter with street art, venues and the coach station. Livelier and cheaper.

food: Try a balti curry: the dish is linked to Birmingham. Expect around £10–15 for a main in the Balti Triangle.
Digbeth and the city centre have street-food markets and food halls; check opening days on the day.
The Jewellery Quarter has independent cafés and bakeries; good for a cheap lunch.
Brindleyplace and the canalside are best for sit-down dinners; book ahead at weekends.
A pint in a traditional pub is a local ritual; prices vary, so check the board.
more_time: Swap a city afternoon for a canal walk or narrowboat trip; the towpaths are flat and free.
Take a short train ride to Stratford-upon-Avon or Warwick for Shakespeare and castle history; check times and fares on the day.
Add a day for the Black Country Living Museum if industrial history interests you; check opening days first.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the museums, the canals and a balti dinner without rushing; add a night for a day trip.

month_notes: Jan: cold, highs near 7°C and about 12 rain days. Pack a warm waterproof coat.
Feb: similar to January, highs around 8°C. Short daylight; plan indoor sights.
Mar: still cool at 10°C with the most rain days (14). Keep an umbrella handy.
Apr: milder at 12°C, around 12 rain days. Good for walking the canals.
May: pleasant at 16°C. A good month for outdoor sightseeing.
Jun: warmer at 19°C, 13 rain days. Long evenings suit canal-side dinners.
Jul: warmest month, highs near 21°C but 14 rain days. Bring a light rain layer.
Aug: similar to July at 20°C with fewer rain days (11). Busy school-holiday crowds.
Sep: mild at 18°C, 13 rain days. Comfortable for museums and markets.
Oct: cooler at 14°C, around 12 rain days. Pack layers.
Nov: chilly at 10°C with 13 rain days. Indoor plans are safest.
Dec: cold at 8°C and 14 rain days. Christmas markets and warm pubs help.

climate_guide.summary: Temperate and changeable: mild summers, cool wet winters, and rain possible in any month.

items.title: Rain all year
items.text: Expect 11–14 rain days every month. Showers are often short; carry a small umbrella.

items.title: Mild summers
items.text: July and August peak near 20–21°C. Rarely hot; evenings cool to about 12°C.

items.title: Cool winters
items.text: January and February highs near 7–8°C, lows around 2°C. A warm coat is essential.

items.title: Best months
items.text: May to September is warmest and brightest, though rain never stops entirely.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a waterproof jacket and comfortable shoes for wet pavements.

items.title: Grey skies are normal
items.text: Overcast days are common. Plan indoor backups like museums and food halls.

transit.best: Walk in the compact centre; use buses or the tram for longer hops.

modes.text: West Midlands Metro trams link the centre with Wolverhampton and Edgbaston; fares are a few pounds.
Frequent National Express West Midlands buses; a Daysaver day ticket costs about £4–5.
Metered taxis; Uber and Bolt both operate in the city.
Easy on motorways but the centre is congested and parking is costly.
The centre is compact and mostly pedestrianised, so walking is best for short trips.
Possible but cycle lanes are few; canal towpaths make pleasant routes.
